title: Authorization landscape: role-graph model and scope/permission matrix for RBAC v2
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: RBAC v1 is flat and coarse-grained. We lack a consistent resource hierarchy, scopes are inconsistent across services, admin controls are scattered, and audit logs are noisy and hard to map back to authorization decisions. Goal: design RBAC v2 role model with a formal resource hierarchy, canonical scope primitives, a permissions matrix that supports least-privilege and temporary elevation, and clear mappings from SSO/SAML groups to roles. Deliverables: spec document, permissions matrix CSV, migration plan, integration tests, audit log schema additions, and a staged rollout with canary enforcement and observability hooks.
proposal_summary: Introduce a role-graph model (roles as nodes, inherits/parents edges) plus resource namespace tree (org > project > cluster > model > route). Define canonical scope primitives (read, write, manage, deploy, impersonate, audit-view) and create a cross-product permission matrix. Roles are assigned to principals at a scope (role binding) rather than globally. Support transient role bindings (timeboxed), SSO group sync mapping, and admin flags for emergency break-glass. Audit logging will record: decision_id, principal, role_binding_id, evaluated_scopes, resource_path, result, reason, and policy_version.
resource_hierarchy: Top-level: organization; children: workspace/project; children: resource pools (dedicated/private); leaf resources: model, route, deployment, dataset; cross-cutting resources: billing-account, secret-store. Examples: org/alpha/project-payments/model/gptx, org/alpha/project-payments/route/chat-endpoint.
scope_definitions: Canonical scopes: read (list/get), write (create/update/delete), manage (modify configuration & bindings), deploy (start/stop/scale), impersonate (act-on-behalf for troubleshooting), audit-view (view audit logs & traces). Compound scopes: read+deploy, manage+audit-view. Scopes are additive and evaluated by least privilege rules.
permissions_matrix_summary: Matrix rows: role types (viewer, operator, developer, deployer, billing-admin, security-admin, super-admin, custom). Columns: canonical scopes applied to resource classes (organization, project, model, route, deployment, billing-account). Each cell: allow/deny/conditional. Conditional examples: operator on deployment at project scope can deploy only if autoscale policy exists; developer has write on model but cannot manage secrets. The matrix will be delivered as a CSV artifact linked below.
migration_plan: Phase 1: read-only analysis of existing bindings, SSO groups, and effective permissions; generate a delta report. Phase 2: create compatible role aliases that map current v1 permissions to v2 role graph with warnings for ambiguous mappings. Phase 3: opt-in canary where enforcement toggles for 5% of orgs; collect enforcement logs, false-positive/negative reports. Phase 4: full enforcement + deprecation of v1 APIs. Provide 'simulate' mode for 30 days to validate. Provide scripts for migrating service accounts and CI tokens.
rollout_plan: Week 0: merge spec and infra prototypes. Week 1-2: implement role-graph core and scope evaluator. Week 3: SSO/SAML group mapping UI + sync. Week 4: audit log schema rollout and observability dashboards. Week 5: start 5% canary, run two weeks, iterate on policy exceptions. Week 8: expand to 50%, then full. Each step gated by acceptance criteria and security review.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical resource hierarchy documented and approved by PM and Security
Permission evaluator implemented with unit and integration tests covering >95% cases
Migration tool produces non-empty delta report for all existing orgs in staging
Audit logs include decision_id, role_binding_id, evaluated_scopes, policy_version and are queryable within Console
SSO/SAML group mapping UI present in Console and can be exercised in staging
Canary enforcement completes with <2% critical production impact and documented rollbacks
progress_updates: 2026-02-28: Kickoff meeting with Security, IAM, Console, and Infra. Agreed on role-graph approach and canonical scopes.
2026-03-03: Drafted resource hierarchy and initial permissions matrix; flagged billing-account and secret-store as special cross-cutting resources.
2026-03-06: Prototype scope evaluator implemented; simple policy language POC using expression-based clauses (matches resource_path, scope, time constraints).
2026-03-09: SSO mapping requirements captured; SAML group->role-binding sync design completed. Starting Console UX wireframes.
2026-03-10: Security review scheduled; preparing threat model and audit schema changes for review next week
decisions: Adopt role-graph (DAG) rather than flat roles to allow limited multiple inheritance and avoid cycles
Role bindings are scoped (role + resource_path + optional time window). No global role assignments except super-admin and billing-admin by default
Introduce transient/timeboxed bindings for emergency/debugging with mandatory justification and audit recording
SSO/SAML group sync maps to role bindings; groups can be mapped to multiple bindings but mappings require owner approval
Audit logs must include policy_version and decision_id to enable reproducible lookups
implementation_steps: Add resource_path canonicalizer in infra to normalize incoming requests
Build role-graph storage (Dynamo table) with efficient ancestor/descendant queries
Implement evaluator that accepts principal, requested_scope, resource_path and returns allow/deny with reason and decision_id
Extend audit payload to include role_binding_id and policy_version; wire into existing event pipeline
Console: add role binding CRUD and SSO group mapping UI; add simulator mode to preview effective permissions
Migration: write scanner to infer candidate role mappings from v1 bindings and produce human-reviewable CSV
Testing: unit tests for scope combinations, integration tests with SAML IdP in staging, chaos tests for race conditions in transient bindings
risks: Mis-mapped SSO groups leading to over-privilege; mitigated by require owner approval and simulation period
Performance regression in auth evaluation on high QPS routes; mitigated by caching decisions (TTL) and prefix/KV cache on resource_path
Audit volume increase could exceed retention/ingest budgets; will add sampling for high-frequency non-security events and index keys for common queries
Backward-compatibility gaps for some service accounts used by legacy CI; include migration scripts and manual rollback instructions
